intended_object: The canonical isomorphism 𝒪^{(I)} ⊗ 𝒪^{(I')} ≅ 𝒪^{(I×I')}: the tensor product of the free sheaves of modules on I and on I' (over a sheaf of commutative rings R on a small site) is the free sheaf of modules on I × I'. Under it, the generator e_{(i,i')} goes to e_i ⊗ e_{i'}. I took this from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
This is a canonical isomorphism, not an arbitrary one. The proof is the standard one.
- `free I` is the coproduct of copies of the unit indexed by I.
- Tensoring with a fixed object preserves coproducts (`isColimitCofanMkObjOfIsColimit` applied to `tensorLeft` and `tensorRight`).
- So `free I ⊗ free I'` is a coproduct indexed by I × I' of the objects `unit ⊗ unit`, combined with `Cofan.IsColimit.prod`.
- Each `unit ⊗ unit` is identified with `unit` through the left unitor.
- Comparing with the colimit cofan of `free (I × I')` gives the isomorphism.

The companion lemma `ιFree_freeTensorFreeIso_inv` confirms what the docstring says: the generator (i, i') goes to λ⁻¹ ≫ (ιFree i ⊗ ιFree i'), i.e. e_i ⊗ e_{i'}. So the definition carries the intended map, not merely some isomorphism.

On generality: the setting (a small site, a sheaf of commutative rings, index types in the same universe u) is the one in which the library's monoidal structure on sheaves of modules is built, so it is the natural setting here. The closest thing in Mathlib is the module-level fact `finsuppTensorFinsupp'`. I found no sheaf-level version in Mathlib.
